title: Experiences in Makespan Minimization Using Deep Reinforcement Learning for R||Cmax
content: Much progress has been made in the scheduling theory, approximate solutions, complexity aspects, and practical algorithms. After the year 2012 we started seeing the applications of deep neural networks and deep reinforcement learning to the domain of scheduling. A literature survey indicates that most of the applications are related to jobs shop scheduling having different problems scenarios such as job families, machine families, due dates, release dates, arrival time constraints etc.We study the case of unrelated parallel machines, see a review the progress made in this area in (11). In this paper, we report our experience in using deep reinforcement learning (DRL) to minimize the makespan for unrelated parallel machine scheduling (UPMS). Additional references to recent progress is also addressed.
